description: The broker's own fee for executing the order.
Levied on the value of the trade. Not a taxable service, so it never forms part of a GST base.
Charged by the exchange on turnover. NSE and BSE differ, which is why a rate card may name an exchange.

statutoryReference: SEBI (Regulatory Fee on Stock Exchanges) Regulations, 2006

description: Levied on purchases only. Not a taxable service, so it never forms part of a GST base.
Levied once per scrip per day per demat account on a sell, however many transactions make it up.
A percentage of the taxable services only. The rule must name its base codes explicitly; securities transaction tax and stamp duty are never among them.
Billed per demat account on a cycle rather than on a trade.
One-off charge when an account is opened.
Levied by the scheme, not the broker, and depends on how long each redeemed lot was held. Belongs on an instrument profile rather than a rate card.
Distributor transaction fee, applicable only to regular plans.
